newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes higher on late dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes higher on late dlr sales.

text.p: The Philippine peso gained more strength on Wednesday after a bank sold dollars at 26.372 to the U.S. dollar in late trading, Traders said.
They suspected that the $15 million were bought by the Central Bank which had been seen buying back dollars at 26.373 on Tuesday to beef up its reserves.
"Aside from that, the market was relatively quiet for the whole day," one trader said. Total turnover was lean at $113.9 million.
The peso was stuck in a tight range of 26.373 and 26.374 through most of the session.

Traders said the announcement of a two percentage point rate cut in the overnight reverse repo rate, the benchmark for the interbank call loan market, did not stir any activity in the foreign exchange market.
"As long as the Central Bank keeps its selling rate at 26.375, I don't think the peso will move down beyond that rate," another trader said.
Traders were expecting peso to remain steady at the current levels.
